# Bättre än väntat från Nibe – börsen mot dyster inledning

**Feed**: efn-borsfrukost  
**Published**: 2026-11-17  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

EFN Morgon on 17 November 2026 centres on Nibe's Q3 report, which beat expectations. Operating margin came in at 13.6% against 12.7% expected, Climate Solutions reached a 15.7% margin with capacity utilisation at only about 60%, and Elements was lifted by semiconductor demand. Guests Anders Roslund (Pareto) and Lukas Mattsson (Indires) call the report a sign of quality but see the AI/datacenter sell-off hitting ABB, Atlas Copco, Alfa Laval and Munters. They also discuss the SKF/Vertevo spin-off, the Pricer takeover bid, a weak, uneven consumer pressured by rising rates, and lower copper prices pulling the miners down on a gloomy Stockholm opening.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 NIBE-B — Nibe | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Q3 beat; Climate Solutions margin 15.7% at only ~60% utilisation; guest sees the stock as interesting at current levels with room for further margin gains

#### Reasoning

Both guests call it a strong report that signals quality. Margins held up despite fears of overcapacity and price pressure, and higher utilisation (70-80%) could lift margins further. Elements gains from semiconductor demand. Falling debt could reopen acquisitions. Anders is more cautious: after a 30% rise, expectations were already high, so he is only 'lite svagt positivt'.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Climate Solutions margins fall due to overcapacity/price pressure
- if higher interest rates hit consumer heat pump demand
- if semiconductor demand in Elements weakens

> *"då tycker jag ändå att ni blir intressanta på de här nivåerna ändå"*

---

### 🟡 SKF-B — SKF | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest: the long-term story is owning SKF, but the remaining company carries restructuring costs and capex needs

#### Reasoning

The Pareto guest says owning SKF is the long-term case. However, the remaining SKF has high restructuring costs and large capital needs, so it mainly has to deliver stable, slow progress. Vertevo may offer more upside.

#### Sell Triggers

- if restructuring costs escalate
- if the Vertevo spin-off destroys value

> *"den långsiktiga storyn är ju att äga SKF"*

---

### ⛔ NOBI — Nobia | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Q3 report loser in capital goods with a long tough period; rising rates are hitting the consumer

#### Reasoning

The guest lists Nobia among companies selling postponable, capital-heavy purchases that have struggled for a long time. Rising rates and a weak consumer make things worse. This is implied rather than an explicit recommendation.

#### Sell Triggers

- if consumer confidence and interest rates improve clearly

> *"Det är ju Nobia, Husqvarna, Electrolux till viss del också"*
